verifications.note: NextEra fact sheet for the Paducah American Energy Hub. It says McCracken County, natural gas generation of up to 2,000 MW, and commercial operation as early as 2032.
WKMS public radio story of July 29, 2026. It says NextEra will build gas-fired power near the former Paducah Gaseous Diffusion Plant in McCracken County.
Kentucky Lantern story of July 29, 2026. It says NextEra will install two gigawatts of natural gas-fired generation at or near the former Paducah plant in McCracken County.

records.researcher_notes: GEM does not list this plant. NextEra Energy Resources and the Department of Energy announced on July 29, 2026 a large data center and power project at the former Paducah Gaseous Diffusion Plant in McCracken County. NextEra's fact sheet says the project includes natural gas generation of up to 2,000 MW, with commercial operation as early as 2032. A WKMS radio story and a Kentucky Lantern story of the same day say the same. No air permit application or siting board case was found yet, so the status is announced. The point is the former plant site and is approximate, because the fact sheet says the plant will be at or near it. The owner name is spelled as it already is in the GEM entity list. GEM's Shawnee Fossil Plant and the Paducah Power plant are in the same county but are different plants. Technology is combined cycle. It rests on one source, a quote from the head of Greater Paducah Economic Development in a WPSD Local 6 story from the announcement day. NextEra's FAQ page says the gas plant needs water to cool its power-generating units, which fits a combined cycle plant but does not name it. No turbine maker or model has been made public. No air permit application, siting board case or Public Service Commission case was found as of November 7, 2026, and a project tracker at americanbuildout.com said the same on September 27, 2026.

East Kentucky Power Cooperative's 2025 resource plan, filed April 1, 2025 in Kentucky commission case 2025-00087, lists its planned additions in Table 1-4 in the executive summary: 214 MW of engines in 2029 and the 745 MW Cooper combined cycle in 2031. It has no plant in Mason County and nothing near 780 MW, so it predates this request. A web search for the request number, East Kentucky Power Cooperative and Mason County found no news story, company announcement or turbine order that says combined cycle, simple cycle, peaker or engines.

records.plant_name: TenKey Franklin Data Center power station

verifications.note: WKU Public Radio story by Lisa Autry, published October 22, 2025. It says a deed for 529 acres on Steele Road was recorded to TenKey Land Company, LLC on May 15, 2025, and that "The data center would be powered by natural gas turbines."

WKU Herald story "Data Center Dilemma", published April 7, 2026. It says TenKey LandCo LLC proposed a data center near 421 Steele Road, Franklin, that would use "on-site power generation via clean natural gas turbines" and not connect to the city grid.

WKU Public Radio story of March 4, 2026. It says the Franklin Planning and Zoning Commission voted unanimously to approve the preliminary development plan of TenKey LandCo, LLC for three 200,000 square foot buildings off Exit 2 on Steele Road "with on-site power manufacturing".
WKMS story of January 28, 2026. It says TenKey sued the Simpson County government over the county land use ordinance for data centers.
Data Center Dynamics story on the March 2026 approval of the TenKey plan in Franklin, which names natural gas power on site.

Signed minutes of the Franklin Planning and Zoning Commission, March 3, 2026, read by text recognition. Page 2 records the unanimous vote to approve the Preliminary Development Plan of TenKey LandCo I LLC for "a data storage and service center with power manufacturing located at 421 Steele Road", on condition that the power generation stays an ancillary use and is not sold.

Signed minutes of the Franklin Planning and Zoning Commission special meeting, February 5, 2026, read by text recognition. Page 1 records a commissioner asking "who will regulate the power and the gas turbines", and TenKey's attorney saying the power is generated only for the data center. The plan was tabled that night.

Franklin Planning and Zoning Commission agenda for January 8, 2026, the earliest posted record of the application: "TenKey LandCo I LLC to request a preliminary development plan for a data storage and service center with power manufacturing located at 421 Steele Road."

records.researcher_notes: GEM does not list this plant. It was found in the final internet check of the Kentucky batch on November 7, 2026. TenKey bought 529 acres on Steele Road in Franklin, Simpson County, in May 2025, and plans three data center buildings powered by its own natural gas turbines with battery storage, off the city grid. WKU Public Radio first reported the gas turbines on October 22, 2025 (fourth paragraph). The WKU Herald story of April 7, 2026 quotes the company website on "on-site power generation via clean natural gas turbines". The Franklin Planning and Zoning Commission approved the preliminary plan on March 3, 2026 (WKU Public Radio, March 4, 2026, first paragraph). No source gives the number or size of the turbines, so capacity is left blank, as the manual allows. The Kentucky air permit system had no application from TenKey as of November 5, 2026, but the city's own records show a land use application: the Franklin Planning and Zoning Commission agenda of January 8, 2026 lists TenKey LandCo I LLC's request for a preliminary development plan for "a data storage and service center with power manufacturing located at 421 Steele Road", and the signed minutes of March 3, 2026 (page 2) record the unanimous approval. A zoning or development plan application counts as the pre-construction step, so the status is pre-construction, dated January 2026, with two publishers (the city minutes and WKU Public Radio). The February 5, 2026 minutes (page 1) record a commissioner asking who will regulate "the gas turbines". The city commission approved an agreement with TenKey Landco, LLC and TenKey Roadco, LLC on July 27, 2026 (city minutes, page 397). The point is the Census geocode of 421 Steele Road, which the WKU Herald names as the site; it is approximate because the campus covers about 200 acres. The owner is new to GEM: the deed names TenKey Land Company, LLC and the planning record names TenKey LandCo, LLC; the shorter name is used. No other GEM plant is in Simpson County. A map pin for the point: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=36.66485,-86.56748

records.researcher_notes: GEM does not list this plant. It was found on November 7, 2026, when the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory queue file gave the first public view of the TVA queue for this batch; the TVA queue site itself needs a sign-in. TVA's own queue list of January 2025 (page 2, Kentucky table, request 628) and the Berkeley Lab file (tab 03, the row for TVA request 628) both show a 1,600 MW gas request in Todd County on the Paradise to Montgomery 500 kV line, due June 1, 2030. The two are copies of one TVA queue, so they count as one source. Searches of news, the Kentucky commission, the Kentucky air permit system and TVA's pages found no developer, site or turbine type. TVA's only announced Todd County work is the Stokes switching station near Trenton, which is a transmission project. The queue does not name the developer, so the owner is left blank. The point is the middle of Todd County and is approximate; the 500 kV line crosses the west of the county. Google Maps: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=36.84,-87.18
